proof_summary: Finite prime-decomposition tables handle the bounded ranges, while above the thresholds a positive term supplies a prime \(q\) whose complementary prime gives \(n=(n-q)+q\) in the even case and \(n=(n-2q)+2q\) in the odd case. Applying the even case to \(n=2(N+4007)\), the bound \(2q<n\) makes the cousin-prime pair \((n-q-6,n-q)\) exceed any prescribed \(N\), proving infinitude.
